Senses.PreferredTarget: to pick out and bring forward
Senses.Note: The old word-versus-object split failed guide item 8: object choice and figurative or literal reading do not create different referents when the same predicate frame survives. Relation witnesses preserve three neighboring verbs without treating them as definitions: Zhuanyu Heng forbids carelessly picking up old worthies' encounters, Wumen Huikai names the printing of forty-eight cases for picking up and presenting, and Yuanwu Keqin places raising the old and present beside putting material to one side. Senses.Explanation: To pick out and bring forward is a public, transitive action in these records: something is selected or taken up and put where others can hear, see, inspect, or receive it. Zhenjing Kewen brings Mazu's Sun-Face Buddha and Moon-Face Buddha wording forward again for his audience (日面佛，月面佛，一一為君重拈出). Duanqiao Miaolun says he must bring out one phrase so that what heaven and humanity have not heard or seen may be heard and seen (拈出一句子，使天上人間未聞者聞、未見者見). Gaofeng Yuanmiao brings an old doubt forward again from the beginning in a letter (今日重疑，不免從頭拈出), and Lu Hang asks that the cases of the various houses not be brought forward before requesting one direct phrase (諸家因緣，不勞拈出). The same verb governs presented objects. Pufeng Haidong tells an unnamed monk who claims to have a jewel, “try bringing it out and let us see” (試拈出看). Baichi Yuan says he will take a bright pearl from inside his robe and present it before the assembly (不免乘時拈出，對眾分付). Tian'an Sheng and Yongji Rong bring out incense for public offering. These are not two different headword senses: phrases, cases, doubts, jewels, pearls, and incense are different direct objects of one selecting-and-presenting action. Chan bends that action into a standard verb for putting inherited cases and a participant's claimed answer into the public exchange, while retaining its use for objects physically displayed and offered.
